azure-devops.notes: Run CRLF detection early in pipeline before other checks.

core.description: Enforce line endings at the Git layer using .gitattributes. Mark text files with appropriate EOL handling (eol=lf for shell scripts, eol=auto for most files) and binary files as binary to prevent corruption. This prevents 'works locally, fails in CI' issues caused by CRLF/LF mismatches.
core.label: Git Attributes (Line Endings)

machineCheck.description: Verify no CRLF in Python files

stack.notes: Python files should use LF endings for cross-platform compatibility. Mark *.py as eol=lf in .gitattributes. Shebang scripts fail with CRLF.
stack.verification: Run 'git ls-files --eol' and verify Python files use LF.

azure-devops.notes: Run CRLF detection as the first quality check before linting or testing.

core.description: Fail CI early for Linux-executed files containing CRLF line endings. Shell scripts, Python files, and other interpreted files fail silently or with cryptic errors when they contain \r characters. Detect this before running deeper CI steps.
core.label: CRLF Detection in CI

stack.notes: Python shebang scripts fail with CRLF. Check all .py and .sh files for CRLF before running pytest or other Python tools.
stack.verification: Run CRLF detection on Python and shell files.

stack.verification: .gitignore must exist; .dockerignore is recommended when containerizing or using Docker workflows.

core.description: Use MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH versioning with clear rules and automated changelog generation based on commit history. Maintain a single canonical version source (for example, package.json or VERSION) that all release artifacts use.

stack.notes: Automate version bumping and changelog generation using setuptools_scm (git-tag based) or bumpversion with towncrier for changelog fragments. Keep pyproject.toml (or VERSION) as the single canonical version source, and have CI publish GitHub/PyPI/Docker artifacts from that same version.
stack.verification: Check that the canonical version in pyproject.toml or VERSION follows SemVer and verify that the configured tool (for example, setuptools_scm or bumpversion) computes or bumps the version and generates changelog entries from commit history or fragments.

azure-devops.notes: Run the version guard in PR validation jobs before merge.

core.description: If semantic-release or automated versioning is enabled, block manual edits to canonical version fields in pull requests. Enforce a CI guard (and optional pre-push hook) that fails when version lines change outside the release workflow.
core.label: Version Guard (Automated Releases)

stack.notes: Block manual edits to version fields in pyproject.toml or setup.cfg when automated release tooling computes versions from commit history.
stack.verification: Run the guard and confirm it fails when version lines change in pyproject.toml or setup.cfg.

azure-devops.notes: Ensure format:check step uses ignore file that excludes release artifacts.

core.description: Exclude auto-generated release artifacts (CHANGELOG.md, package-lock.json, etc.) from code formatters to prevent CI failures. Release automation tools generate files that may not conform to your formatter's style, causing format checks to fail on subsequent CI runs.
core.label: Release Artifact Formatter Exclusion

stack.notes: In pyproject.toml [tool.black] or [tool.ruff], add extend-exclude patterns for auto-generated files like CHANGELOG.md. Some versioning tools generate or modify files that should not be reformatted.
stack.verification: Run 'black --check .' or 'ruff format --check' and confirm generated files are excluded.

core.description: Use a single CI release pipeline that publishes all artifacts (GitHub releases, packages, containers) from the same canonical version source.

stack.verification: Trigger the release pipeline and confirm all artifacts share the same version number and tag.

azure-devops.notes: Set HUSKY=0 or equivalent in release pipeline to disable hooks.

core.description: Release automation must bypass local developer hooks (HUSKY=0, --no-verify) and rely solely on CI gates for validation. This ensures idempotent, reproducible releases that don't fail due to hook environment differences.
core.label: Release Hook Bypass

stack.notes: Set PRE_COMMIT_ALLOW_NO_CONFIG=1 or SKIP=all to bypass pre-commit hooks in release automation. CI gates already validated.
stack.verification: Check release workflow for pre-commit bypass.

core.description: Enforce structured commit messages such as Conventional Commits via commit-msg hooks and CI. This is required for deterministic versioning and changelog generation.

core.description: Automatic code formatting to maintain a consistent style across all contributors.

bazelHints.notes: Wrap black as a py_binary run target for format checking.

stack.notes: Use black (or an equivalent opinionated formatter) and treat its output as the single source of truth for code style.
stack.verification: Run the configured formatter (for example, `black .` or `black --check .`) and confirm it reports clean formatting on committed code and auto-fixes as expected locally.

azure-devops.notes: Hooks and CI must invoke identical verification commands. Use npm run verify or equivalent.

core.description: Use git hooks to run linting, formatting, and commit linting before changes are committed. Hooks should CHECK by default (not auto-fix), be fast, and scope to changed files only. Use a single entry hook mechanism (e.g., Husky as entry point calling pre-commit or lint-staged).
core.label: Pre-Commit Hooks

stack.notes: Use pre-commit framework as both entry and executor. Pin hook versions in .pre-commit-config.yaml for determinism. Hooks should run checks (ruff check, black --check) not auto-fix. Run pre-commit install to set up hooks.
stack.verification: Inspect .pre-commit-config.yaml and confirm hooks use check/verify flags, not auto-fix.

azure-devops.notes: CI should call the same verify script that hooks use locally.

core.description: Local hooks and CI must invoke identical verification commands to prevent 'works locally, fails in CI' issues. Use a single canonical verify entrypoint (e.g., npm run verify) that both hooks and CI call.
core.label: Hook/CI Parity

stack.notes: Define a verify target (make verify, tox -e lint, or nox -s lint) that both pre-commit and CI invoke. Pin tool versions in pyproject.toml.
stack.verification: Compare hook commands with CI commands and confirm they invoke the same targets.

azure-devops.notes: Also run secret scanning in CI as a safety net for commits that bypassed hooks.

core.description: Scan staged diffs for credentials, API keys, and secrets before they reach the remote repository. Catch secrets at commit time rather than after they're pushed.

stack.notes: Add detect-secrets or gitleaks to .pre-commit-config.yaml. Use detect-secrets audit to manage baselines.
stack.verification: Run 'detect-secrets scan' or 'gitleaks protect' and verify scanning works.

core.description: Use static type checking to catch errors before runtime and enforce strictness on new code. For JS/TS stacks, require a TypeScript-first policy with strict mode and a CI typecheck step; allow JSDoc/checkJs migration for legacy JS.
core.label: Type Checking

core.description: Lock dependencies and scan regularly for known vulnerabilities; fail CI on newly introduced high-severity issues.

stack.notes: Pin dependency versions and routinely scan for vulnerabilities, prioritizing fixes for critical and high-severity issues.
stack.verification: Dependency lockfile is present; security scanning is configured in CI or project tooling.

core.description: Ensure builds are reproducible by pinning dependencies, base images, and tool/runtime versions. Avoid network/time variance and fail when lockfiles drift.

stack.notes: Use pinned lockfiles (requirements.txt or poetry.lock) and pin Python version (.python-version or tool-versions). Avoid non-deterministic installs in CI.
stack.verification: Lockfile is present and CI installs with pinned versions only. Python runtime is pinned.

stack.notes: Use shared CI templates for lint/test/typecheck/release stages to standardize across Python repos.

stack.notes: Define exclude patterns in pyproject.toml [tool.ruff], [tool.black], [tool.mypy] sections. Document why each path is excluded. Avoid runtime --exclude flags.
stack.verification: Review pyproject.toml and confirm all exclusions are defined there, not in scripts.

migrationGuide.description: Add pre-commit hooks with secret scanning, formatting, and linting. Hooks should CHECK (not auto-fix) and scope to changed files only for speed.

migrationGuide.description: Introduce CI quality gates that mirror local hooks exactly. Add CRLF detection early in pipeline. Treat existing violations as warnings where possible.
migrationGuide.notes: CI must call the same verify scripts that hooks use. Add CRLF detection before other checks to fail fast on line ending issues. Use diff-based tools so only new violations break builds.

migrationGuide.description: Enable type-checking, coverage thresholds, and dependency/vulnerability scanning with gradual enforcement.
